solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woman in Congress almost completely mad

definitions.note: a playful noun: congress here is sexual intercourse, so the woman so engaged is one who bonks

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: bonkers is slang for completely mad

explanation.surface: A female politician on Capitol Hill is said to be nearly out of her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' is not the US legislature but the old word for sexual union; 'bonk' is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky coinage: someone engaged in bonking, British slang for sex, which 'congress' also means.

clue.text: Amateurish jewellery you wear on your bottom?

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about body jewellery worn on the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumbling describes someone clumsy and inept, as an unskilled novice would be.

clue.text: He fancied himself a handsome chap in bed

definitions.meaning: the youth of Greek myth fell in love with his own reflection
a flower in a garden bed, named after that beautiful youth

explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth who loved his own reflection gave his name to the daffodil family flower.

clue.text: Garden delighted English nurses

indicators.note: nurses means holds or cradles, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: A happy English nurse tends a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' is a verb: the two words cradle the answer across their join.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived is the garden of God.

clue.text: Philosopher makes old actress sad

indicators.note: sad here is taken as sorry or in a poor state, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker is said to reduce an ageing performer to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian thinker who taught Plato is the archetypal ancient Greek philosopher.

clue.text: Boob half glimpsed, you say? That's awfully rude

indicators.note: half means only part of the word, here its second pair of letters
you say means the words are heard, not read

parts.note: glimpsed means seen

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction is glimpsed, prompting a scandalised cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes OB from 'Boob'; 'you say' turns SEEN into the word that sounds like it, SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensively indecent, an extreme of being rude.

clue.text: Aren't rats dreadful round university cafe?

indicators.note: round means the anagram goes around the next letter
dreadful means in a terrible state, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone complains about rats around a campus cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges AREN'T RATS to RESTARANT; 'round' places U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a small eating place, a kind of dining establishment.

clue.text: Time to get behind the President

parts.note: the rump is the behind or backside

explanation.surface: A call that it is time to support the President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' reads as 'supporting'; it is a noun for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump is a US President, the head of state named here.

clue.text: Mountain range in South Africa? I'm mistaken

indicators.note: in puts the confession inside the abbreviation

parts.note: I'm mistaken is I err

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a mountain range is in South Africa, then admits error.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, from the Spanish for saw.

clue.text: Cheerfulness of Italian put in charge

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: a levy is a charge or tax

explanation.surface: An Italian promoted to run things is very cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in charge' reads as promoted; split it, 'charge' is a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is light-hearted humour, a lack of seriousness close to cheerfulness.

clue.text: Her Majesty feeding groups of crows? They've got a taste for blood

definitions.text: They've got a taste for blood

indicators.note: feeding means one element is put into the mouth of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a murder is the collective noun for a flock of crows
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen scatters food for crows, which turn out to be bloodthirsty.
explanation.walkthrough: A flock of crows is called a 'murder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Killers are, figuratively, people with a thirst or taste for blood.

clue.text: Rudeness of reporter's informant

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the word, so we hear it rather than see it spelt

parts.note: a journalist's informant is their source

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark is attributed to a journalist's tipster.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for an informant is said the same as the word for cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is British informal for cheek or impudence, a synonym of rudeness.

clue.text: Put phone back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word backwards

parts.note: to dial is to phone someone

explanation.surface: An instruction to hang up the handset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' looks like part of the phrase 'put back'; it is the definition, as in 'laid the table'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past forms of setting something down: placed it, set it down.

clue.text: Water pipe repair ultimately botched. Bugger!

indicators.note: botched work is messed up, so the letters are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A plumber curses a failed fix on a water pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugger!' reads as an oath; it is a noun, one who plants bugs. 'botched' rearranges WATER PIPE into WIRETAPPE; 'ultimately' adds the last letter of 'repair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugger is one who plants listening devices, which is exactly what a phone eavesdropper does.

clue.text: Huge fuss about Russian leader. He's got his eye on you!

definitions.text: He's got his eye on you!

parts.note: huge means big

indicators.note: about means the word for fuss goes around the letter

parts.note: bother means fuss

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A huge fuss about a Russian politician comes with a warning of surveillance.
explanation.walkthrough: From Orwell's 1984 slogan 'Big Brother is watching you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's all-seeing figurehead watches everyone, a byword for state surveillance.

clue.text: Horribly fizzy wine left in New York

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Some sparkling wine abandoned in Manhattan has gone off horribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe doing something in an unpleasant, nasty way.

clue.text: Mistakes in Cicero's writings?

parts.note: the Latin word for errors is the one a Roman writer like Cicero would use, and it is also a printed list of errors in a book

explanation.surface: A query about slips in the orator's works.
explanation.walkthrough: The English word for a list of corrections is borrowed straight from Latin, Cicero's language.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors in a book, from the Latin plural meaning things gone wrong.

clue.text: Argentine bananas, or some other fruit?

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Are these Argentinian bananas, or some other kind of fruit?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit; it means mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit, a different fruit from the banana.

clue.text: Hostility on ship's uncalled for

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: needle is ill feeling or antagonism, as in a needle match
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Hostility on board a ship is said to be unwarranted.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, not required or warranted.

clue.text: Slippery Boris adopts American line

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the next letter goes inside
slippery suggests something that will not hold its shape, so the letters slide about

explanation.surface: A slippery politician named Boris takes up a US policy line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery' rearranges BORIS to ISOBR, and 'adopts' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal pressure.

clue.text: Order German crime writer to appear first

indicators.note: to appear first places the writer before the abbreviation

parts.note: Ian Rankin is a Scottish crime novelist

explanation.surface: A German crime novelist demands top billing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is an order of position, a placing in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Punishment for article skewering vice president

indicators.note: skewering means running through, so one piece pierces the middle of the other

parts.note: Mike Pence was US Vice President
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece savaging a US vice president is described as a kind of punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper story; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-imposed suffering to atone for a wrong, a form of punishment.

clue.text: Champion swimmer's assistants coming under pressure

indicators.note: coming under places this piece beneath the previous one in the down light

parts.note: helps are assistants or helpers

explanation.surface: An Olympic champion's helpers come under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Phelps is the American swimmer with a record number of Olympic gold medals.

clue.text: Zippy vehicle leaving behind one old duck

indicators.note: leaving behind one means a single copy of the letter is dropped

parts.note: a scooter is a small nippy vehicle

explanation.surface: A scooter rider overtakes an old duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old duck' looks like a British term of endearment for an old woman; 'old' gives O, and 'duck' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Bloody Tory set up!

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for a Conservative or Tory
to set up an organisation is to found it

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that the Conservatives have been framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' suggests being framed; it means established.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild old-fashioned expletive adjectives, as in a damned or blasted nuisance.

clue.text: Nigerian coins new word for song on journey north

indicators.note: on journey north means read upwards in this down light

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: Coins from Nigeria are a fresh topic for a song about travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the currency of Nigeria.

clue.text: Went to get some dope

definitions.meaning: went in the childish sense of having relieved oneself, passed water
dope is slang for cannabis, also called grass

explanation.surface: Someone popped out to buy some drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To wee is to urinate, so the past tense means went to the toilet; it is also slang for cannabis.

clue.text: A bitter constituent

parts.note: reads as a sour voter, but bitter is the British beer and this is one of its ingredients

explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of pale ale; a constituent is an ingredient, not a voter.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried flowers of the hop plant flavour beer and give it its bitterness.

clue.text: Model that's drunk shows a bit of leg

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T can stand for a model
high means intoxicated

explanation.surface: A tipsy catwalk model reveals some leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a fashion model; it is the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper part of the leg, between hip and knee, is a portion of the limb.

clue.text: Jam is better outside!

indicators.note: outside says the word for better wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares that preserves taste better in the open air, or that music is better played outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like fruit preserve; it is the musicians' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To jam is to play music without preparation, making it up on the spot.

clue.text: A violent outburst on the way?

definitions.text: A violent outburst on the way?

parts.words: A violent outburst on the way?
parts.note: read as an outburst that is imminent, but in fact one happening on the road

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way' reads as 'coming soon'; it means on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury at other drivers erupting while motoring is a violent outburst on the road.

clue.text: Judge's son enthralled by clowns

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive within, so the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: asses are fools or clowns

explanation.surface: A judge's boy is captivated by circus clowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge's' reads 'judge is': the definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something is to evaluate or appraise it.
